messages.subject: Response variable distribution assumptions?
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to analyze my point count data using unmarked and have a very general, preliminary question:

I know that the models make no assumptions about the distributions of predictor variables. Do they make assumptions about the distribution of the response (i.e. counts and/or presence/absence data)?

Thanks,
Vlad

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Response variable distribution assumptions?
parts:
Dear Vlad,

 

OH YES !

 

Typical assumptions are Bernoulli for detection/nondetection (a.k.a., “presence/absence”) data and something like a Poisson, zero-inflated Poisson, Negative Binomial, zero-inflated NB, Conway-Maxwell Poisson or some other discrete-valued distribution for counts (a.k.a., “abundance data”). Not all of those are implemented in unmarked though.

 

Best regards  -- Marc
